open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock and elapsed-clock precedence for viewer entry
open_points.text: “that one instant supplies … every current-time comparison that decides the validity of those writes” and CLK-002’s “that instant decides every current-time comparison it makes” conflict with “the elapsed clock … measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of A25 only”
open_points.question: For a viewer-entry request whose rate-limit decision determines whether a session may be written, is that decision made from the operation’s wall-clock instant or from the elapsed-clock reading, and is the rate limiter an explicit exception to the wall-clock rule?
options: The elapsed reading exclusively decides the rate-limit window as an exception to the wall-clock comparison rule
The wall-clock instant decides whether entry is allowed, despite the later elapsed-clock rule
Both readings participate, with an unspecified precedence
open_points.default_guess: Treat the elapsed reading as an explicit exception for the A25 rate-limit decision.

witness.initial: A viewer credential is valid, and the viewer-entry rate-limit window is exactly at its boundary.
events: The viewer submits an entry request.
The operation reads its wall-clock instant and the rate limiter reads its elapsed-clock value.
The two readings place the request on opposite sides of their respective boundary calculations.
outcomes: The elapsed-clock rule admits the request and a viewer session is created.
The every-current-time-comparison rule uses the wall instant and refuses the request.
witness.observer: The viewer and the persisted session store

open_points.subject: CLK-002 wall-reading cardinality
open_points.text: CLK-002 says “an operation takes one wall reading,” while the normative rule limits the read to “An operation … for its own timestamps,” and the Required tests narrow coverage to “a test per operation that reads the wall clock.”
open_points.question: Must every portal operation, including read-only operations and operations that neither compare current time nor write timestamps, take exactly one wall reading, or only operations that need current time?
options: Every operation takes exactly one wall reading
Only an operation that needs a current-time comparison or portal-owned timestamp takes one reading
Timestamp-writing operations read once, while comparison-only operations follow another unstated rule
open_points.default_guess: Only operations that need current time take one wall reading; operations that do not need it take none.

witness.initial: A valid staff session exists and a read-only operation can answer entirely from already authorized and persisted data without creating an audit record.
events: The staff member performs the read-only operation.
outcomes: The operation takes one wall-clock reading because CLK-002 says every operation does.
The operation takes no wall-clock reading because it has no timestamp or current-time decision of its own.
witness.observer: A counting clock source and the operation test suite

open_points.subject: CLK-002 verification of reuse for every comparison
open_points.text: CLK-002 requires that the one instant “decides every current-time comparison it makes,” but its Required tests check read counts and only the particular boundary “an expiry equal to that reading is refused.”
open_points.question: What Required test demonstrates, for every operation and every current-time comparison it performs, that the comparison uses the unchanged single wall reading rather than a derived, cached, or otherwise altered value?
options: Exercise every current-time comparison at its boundary using the injected reading
Define one shared comparison authority whose focused test proves all callers receive the unchanged reading
Regard the counting-clock test and one generic expiry-boundary example as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Exercise each distinct current-time comparison at its boundary with the single injected reading.

witness.initial: An operation reads the injected wall clock once and checks a persisted expiry other than the expiry case covered by the named boundary test.
events: The operation receives wall time T from the counting source.
Its implementation compares the record against T plus a small adjustment without reading a clock again.
outcomes: All stated CLK-002 tests pass because there was exactly one read and the separately tested expiry case refuses at equality, although this comparison violates the invariant.
A test binding this comparison to T fails and exposes the violation.
witness.observer: The invariant test suite and a caller at the affected expiry boundary

open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: The Required tests section binds only “CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]” and “CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]”; no `[witness: ...]` binds the CLK-002 Required tests item.
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and will assert its source restriction, wall-clock read counts, audit-writer exception, elapsed-clock confinement, and viewer-entry boundary behavior?
options: Bind one existing check covering all CLK-002 obligations
Bind separate existing checks for source restrictions, wall-clock operations, and viewer entry
Declare that CLK-002 intentionally has no witness despite the State 2 handoff rule
open_points.default_guess: Bind separate focused checks for the source restriction, operation wall-clock behavior, and elapsed-clock viewer-entry behavior.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 representation of source-supplied instants
open_points.text: The normative rule says source-supplied times keep “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC,” while the CLK-001 Required test says each supplied time “is stored as supplied.”
open_points.question: When a permitted source representation is offset-aware or has a non-UTC offset, must the test expect literal representation preservation or conversion to the equivalent offset-naive UTC value?
options: Preserve the instant but normalize its stored representation to offset-naive UTC
Persist the datetime exactly as represented by the source
Reject every source representation that is not already offset-naive UTC
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the instant and normalize the stored representation to offset-naive UTC.

witness.initial: A source supplies an accepted timestamp representing 10:00 UTC as 12:00+02:00.
events: The portal accepts the source publication and persists its supplied timestamp.
outcomes: The record stores offset-naive 10:00, following the persisted-representation rule.
The record stores 12:00+02:00 literally, following the Required test’s “stored as supplied” wording.
witness.observer: A repository reader and the CLK-001 test

open_points.subject: A32 OSV copy acquisition boundary
open_points.text: OSV data is “read once in that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data,” and an advisory added, changed or withdrawn “after that read” is deferred to the next deploy, but the text does not define the boundary of a read that may require multiple requests or pages.
open_points.question: What makes the OSV data one coherent copy, and at what instant is an advisory considered to have been added, changed, or withdrawn after the read?
options: Use an immutable OSV snapshot identified by a version or digest
Treat all responses fetched during one traversal as one copy even if OSV changes during the traversal
Define the copy at the start of acquisition
Define the copy at completion of acquisition and retry or fail if consistency cannot be proved
open_points.default_guess: Require an immutable snapshot or fail the deploy when one coherent version cannot be established.

witness.initial: The built image contains distribution D version V; acquiring the PyPI ecosystem data requires multiple responses.
events: The deploy begins reading OSV data.
OSV adds an advisory affecting D version V after the first response but before the final response.
outcomes: The advisory is deemed added after the read began and is deferred; the image starts.
The advisory is part of the copy completed during this deploy and blocks the image.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of the service image

open_points.subject: A32 OSV package and version matching
open_points.text: A distribution is vulnerable when an OSV entry “lists its installed version as affected,” and the Required test says “unmatchable advisory data” does not start the service, without defining name normalization, version interpretation, range evaluation, or what counts as unmatchable.
open_points.question: How are an installed distribution and version matched to an OSV PyPI package and affected-version expression, and which matching uncertainties fail the whole deploy?
options: Use OSV/PyPI canonical package-name and version semantics, failing only when an entry relevant to an installed distribution cannot be evaluated
Require literal package-name and version matches
Fail on any malformed or unmatchable entry anywhere in the downloaded PyPI data, including unrelated packages
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical PyPI name and version semantics and fail when data potentially relevant to an installed distribution cannot be evaluated.

witness.initial: The image contains distribution `Foo_Bar` version V; OSV names package `foo-bar` and expresses affected versions as a range containing V.
events: The deploy compares the installed inventory with its OSV copy.
outcomes: Canonical PyPI matching identifies the package and blocks the deploy.
Literal matching treats the names as different and starts the service.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of the vulnerable image

open_points.subject: DEP-002 image identity binding
open_points.text: The Required test requires the verdict to be “bound to that image’s content id” and rejects a verdict “about another image,” but no text defines `content id`.
open_points.question: Which immutable image identity must the vulnerability verdict bind to, especially for multi-platform images and mutable tags?
options: OCI manifest digest for the exact deployed platform image
OCI index digest for a multi-platform image
Image configuration digest
A registry tag or deployment-system build identifier
open_points.default_guess: Bind the verdict to the immutable manifest digest of the exact platform image that will start.

witness.initial: A mutable tag identifies image A when checked and image B when the service is started; the two images have different installed distributions.
events: The release gate checks the tag and records a verdict under one chosen notion of content identity.
The tag is moved to image B.
outcomes: A digest binding detects that B was not checked and refuses to start it.
A tag or build-label binding treats the verdict as applying and starts B.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of image B

open_points.subject: A32 carried deployment procedure
open_points.text: “The tool that runs the check is a deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route.”
open_points.question: Which receiving state owns that deployment procedure, what decided execution must it implement to acquire the one OSV copy and bind the verdict to the exact image, and what check confirms the handoff rather than leaving the tool choice open as ‘later’?
options: Name a receiving state and a concrete procedure contract confirmed by the dependency release-gate check
Declare the Factory deployment route itself as the receiver and specify its executable contract and confirmation
Leave tool and procedure selection to an unspecified later deploy implementation
open_points.default_guess: Name the deployment-route owner and carry a concrete executable contract confirmed by `verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal`.
